questions.stem: An indwelling catheter in a hand vein produces localized redness, and the adjacent vein contains a clot with wall inflammation. This combination is best described as which condition?

explanation.summary: Trauma from an indwelling catheter injures the venous endothelium, promoting inflammation and clot formation within a superficial vein, i.e., superficial thrombophlebitis, typically presenting as a tender, red, cord-like vessel.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trauma from an indwelling catheter injures the venous endothelium, promoting inflammation and clot formation within a superficial vein, i.e., superficial thrombophlebitis, typically presenting as a tender, red, cord-like vessel.

questions.stem: This three-circle diagram shows the central overlap of endothelial damage, a hypercoagulable state, and abnormal blood flow. The central intersection represents the outcome favored when all three coexist. Clinically, which scenario most directly reflects this concept?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Postoperative immobility plus a vessel injury and inherited clotting tendency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hemolysis from a mechanical valve alone

explanation.summary: The figure depicts Virchow triad: endothelial injury, hypercoagulability, and stasis (abnormal flow). Convergence of these factors, as in an immobile postoperative patient with vessel injury and a thrombophilia, predisposes to venous thrombosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The figure depicts Virchow triad: endothelial injury, hypercoagulability, and stasis (abnormal flow). Convergence of these factors, as in an immobile postoperative patient with vessel injury and a thrombophilia, predisposes to venous thrombosis.

questions.stem: This leg shows a tender, erythematous, indurated cord-like streak with reddish nodularity tracking along the course of a superficial vein. This finding is most consistent with which diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A palpable, tender, red cord following a superficial vein reflects thrombosis with surrounding inflammation of that vein (superficial thrombophlebitis), distinct from the diffuse swelling of DVT or the septal panniculitis of erythema nodosum.
explanation.whyCorrect: A palpable, tender, red cord following a superficial vein reflects thrombosis with surrounding inflammation of that vein (superficial thrombophlebitis), distinct from the diffuse swelling of DVT or the septal panniculitis of erythema nodosum.

questions.stem: A patient's lower legs are shown: one leg has marked distal swelling, skin thickening, and dark discoloration compared with the other. What chronic condition does this appearance most likely represent?

explanation.summary: Long-standing venous hypertension from valvular incompetence produces dependent edema, skin thickening, and hemosiderin/pigment changes of the lower leg, the hallmark of chronic venous insufficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Long-standing venous hypertension from valvular incompetence produces dependent edema, skin thickening, and hemosiderin/pigment changes of the lower leg, the hallmark of chronic venous insufficiency.

questions.stem: The medial ankle and foot show brownish pigmentation, induration, and scaling in a patient with long-standing venous disease. This skin change is best described as?

explanation.summary: Chronic venous hypertension causes red-cell extravasation; breakdown of hemoglobin deposits hemosiderin, giving the characteristic brown pigmentation and eczematous change of stasis dermatitis in the gaiter area.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic venous hypertension causes red-cell extravasation; breakdown of hemoglobin deposits hemosiderin, giving the characteristic brown pigmentation and eczematous change of stasis dermatitis in the gaiter area.

questions.stem: A dilated, tortuous, rope-like subcutaneous vein bulges from the calf of this patient. What is this finding?

explanation.summary: Sustained venous reflux dilates superficial veins into the visible, tortuous, elongated cords known as varicose veins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sustained venous reflux dilates superficial veins into the visible, tortuous, elongated cords known as varicose veins.

questions.stem: Both lower legs show woody induration with confluent purple-brown discoloration and scaling over the gaiter region in advanced venous disease. This end-stage skin/subcutaneous change is termed?

explanation.summary: Chronic venous hypertension drives fibrosis of dermis and subcutaneous fat, producing the firm, hyperpigmented, inverted-champagne-bottle change called lipodermatosclerosis, often preceding venous ulceration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic venous hypertension drives fibrosis of dermis and subcutaneous fat, producing the firm, hyperpigmented, inverted-champagne-bottle change called lipodermatosclerosis, often preceding venous ulceration.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts normal and abnormal venous return in the leg. What underlying defect explains the abnormal (refluxing) blood flow and varicosities shown on the right?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Occlusion of the deep vein by thrombus

explanation.summary: When one-way venous valves fail, blood refluxes distally under gravity, raising venous pressure and dilating superficial veins into varicosities, in contrast with competent valves that direct flow upward.
explanation.whyCorrect: When one-way venous valves fail, blood refluxes distally under gravity, raising venous pressure and dilating superficial veins into varicosities, in contrast with competent valves that direct flow upward.

questions.stem: The illustration shows a needle injecting an agent directly into a superficial vein, with a magnified view of the vein lumen filling with a fibrotic/occluding mass. What treatment does this depict?

explanation.summary: Sclerotherapy injects a chemical sclerosant into the target vein, damaging the endothelium so the vein fibroses and is obliterated, as shown by the occluded lumen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sclerotherapy injects a chemical sclerosant into the target vein, damaging the endothelium so the vein fibroses and is obliterated, as shown by the occluded lumen.

questions.stem: This 4-step sequence shows a catheter introduced and advanced up a vein, then the vein narrowing and closing as the catheter is withdrawn. By what mechanism is the vein closed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The vein is surgically tied off and removed

choices.label: B
choices.text: A metal stent holds the vein permanently open

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thermal energy from the catheter injures the vein wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: A chemical sclerosant is injected into the lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: A clot-dissolving drug is infused to reopen it

explanation.summary: Endovenous thermal (radiofrequency or laser) ablation delivers heat that denatures the vein wall collagen, causing contraction and fibrotic closure as the catheter is slowly withdrawn.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endovenous thermal (radiofrequency or laser) ablation delivers heat that denatures the vein wall collagen, causing contraction and fibrotic closure as the catheter is slowly withdrawn.
